title: Preservation for restricted integral compact support
statement:
theorem integral_support_preservation (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (_hl : l ≠ D.p)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [f.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (c : Compactification f) (E : FieldStage.{u} l) :
    ∀ K : finiteTorConstructibleIntegralCategory l E.carrier X,
      finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l E.carrier Y
        ((PurCompactSupport.image (PurCompactSupport.completed l E.carrier) c).obj K.obj)

source.place: transport of normalized adjunction to full finite-Tor subcategories

proof.text: Install residue-field invertibility by transporting the unit of l in D.k along each residue-field algebra map. Apply integral_residue_tor at X and Y to identify the integral constructibility predicate with finite-Tor constructibility.

Regard K.obj as an object Kprime of sfIntegralConstructibleCategory using the predicate equality. The normalized finite compact-support action supplies sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor and its object property, while sfQcqsCompactSupportRealization identifies its output with the completed compact-support image. Transport that property across the realization isomorphism to obtain sfIntegralConstructible for the image.
Rewrite the output predicate using the equality from integral_residue_tor and conclude the required finiteTorConstructibleIntegral membership.
